Never add a test whose only evidence is that it opens, reads, greps, parses, or
snapshots implementation source code and finds or omits particular strings,
tokens, lines, commands, function names, prompt phrases, regex matches, AST
shapes, or incidental snapshots. That does not prove behavior: matching text
can be dead or commented out, and a behavior-preserving refactor can change it.

Instead execute a public or executable interface and assert observable behavior,
state, output, side effects, and failure modes. For machine-consumed declarative
artifacts such as workflow YAML, JSON, policy, .gitignore, or generated
configuration, invoke the real consumer when feasible or parse into a typed or
normalized semantic model and assert meaning. A raw substring or regex over the
file is still the anti-pattern.

Reading a file is legitimate when the file is itself generated public output, a
serialized protocol, persisted state, an intentional snapshot, or another
explicitly owned text or byte contract. Name that contract, and do not use its
contents as a proxy that unrelated code works. A natural-language prompt or
instruction is not proven effective because its source contains a sentence.
Deterministic CI may test the final emitted prompt delivered to an agent as an
intentional generated interface; model interpretation belongs in
development-only evaluation, not live-LLM CI.

For a regression, reproduce the reported failure when feasible: the test should
fail before the fix and pass after it.

#!/bin/sh
# gh identity router for the no-mistakes daemon and other PATH-based gh
# callers on this host. Routes gh invocations that target kunchenguid/axi or
# any masculinecache/* repository through the masculinecache account
# (GH_CONFIG_DIR=~/.config/gh-masculinecache), per the fleet identity
# decision: contributions owned by masculinecache must never be created or
# mutated with the default phillias credentials (cross-fork PR creation as
# phillias fails with "must be a collaborator"). Everything else passes
# through to the first gh found on PATH (the mise-managed gh on a fresh
# host, the system gh elsewhere). An explicit GH_CONFIG_DIR from the caller
# always wins. No secrets live here; it only selects a config dir.
# Resolve gh from PATH, skipping this script itself to avoid self-recursion:
# PATH may contain ~/.local/bin before the mise shims dir, in which scenario
# "command -v gh" would resolve here. The walk is recursive (no IFS word
# splitting) so PATH entries containing spaces still resolve correctly.
GH=$(command -v gh 2>/dev/null)
_self=$(readlink -f "$0" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "$0")
_walk_path() {
  case "$1" in
    '') return 1 ;;
    *:*) _d=${1%%:*}; _rest=${1#*:} ;;
    *) _d=$1; _rest= ;;
  esac
  if [ -n "$_d" ] && [ -x "$_d/gh" ]; then
    _t=$(readlink -f "$_d/gh" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "$_d/gh")
    if [ "$_t" != "$_self" ]; then
      GH="$_d/gh"; _d=; _rest=; _t=
      return 0
    fi
    _t=
  fi
  _d=
  [ -n "$_rest" ] && _walk_path "$_rest"
}
if [ -z "$GH" ] || [ "$(readlink -f "$GH" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "$GH")" = "$_self" ]; then
  GH=
  _walk_path "$PATH"
fi
if [ -z "$GH" ] || [ ! -x "$GH" ] || [ "$(readlink -f "$GH" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "$GH")" = "$_self" ]; then
  echo "gh: no gh binary found on PATH" >&2
  exit 127
fi
unset _self
if [ -n "$GH_CONFIG_DIR" ]; then
  exec "$GH" "$@"
fi
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    kunchenguid/axi|masculinecache/*)
      GH_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.config/gh-masculinecache"
      export GH_CONFIG_DIR
      exec "$GH" "$@"
      ;;
  esac
done
exec "$GH" "$@"

#!/bin/sh
# gh identity router for the no-mistakes daemon and other PATH-based gh
# callers on this host. Routes gh invocations that target kunchenguid/axi or
# any masculinecache/* repository through the masculinecache account
# (GH_CONFIG_DIR=~/.config/gh-masculinecache), per the fleet identity
# decision: contributions owned by masculinecache must never be created or
# mutated with the default phillias credentials (cross-fork PR creation as
# phillias fails with "must be a collaborator"). Everything else passes
# through to the first gh found on PATH (the mise-managed gh on a fresh
# host, the system gh elsewhere). An explicit GH_CONFIG_DIR from the caller
# always wins. No secrets live here; it only selects a config dir.
# Resolve gh from PATH, skipping this script itself to avoid self-recursion:
# PATH may contain ~/.local/bin before the mise shims dir, in which scenario
# "command -v gh" would resolve here. The walk is recursive (no IFS word
# splitting) so PATH entries containing spaces still resolve correctly.
GH=$(command -v gh 2>/dev/null)
_self=$(readlink -f "$0" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "$0")
_walk_path() {
  case "$1" in
    '') return 1 ;;
    *:*) _d=${1%%:*}; _rest=${1#*:} ;;
    *) _d=$1; _rest= ;;
  esac
  if [ -n "$_d" ] && [ -x "$_d/gh" ]; then
    _t=$(readlink -f "$_d/gh" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "$_d/gh")
    if [ "$_t" != "$_self" ]; then
      GH="$_d/gh"; _d=; _rest=; _t=
      return 0
    fi
    _t=
  fi
  _d=
  [ -n "$_rest" ] && _walk_path "$_rest"
}
if [ -z "$GH" ] || [ "$(readlink -f "$GH" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "$GH")" = "$_self" ]; then
  GH=
  _walk_path "$PATH"
fi
if [ -z "$GH" ] || [ ! -x "$GH" ] || [ "$(readlink -f "$GH" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "$GH")" = "$_self" ]; then
  echo "gh: no gh binary found on PATH" >&2
  exit 127
fi
unset _self
if [ -n "$GH_CONFIG_DIR" ]; then
  exec "$GH" "$@"
fi
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    kunchenguid/axi|masculinecache/*)
      GH_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.config/gh-masculinecache"
      export GH_CONFIG_DIR
      exec "$GH" "$@"
      ;;
  esac
done
exec "$GH" "$@"
